hero.h1: TMJ Treatment in Valencia for Jaw Pain and Headaches
hero.lead: Jaw pain, clicking and tension headaches often trace back to the jaw joint. Dr. Moezzi looks for the cause and treats it with custom appliances, bite correction and whole-body guidance.
hero.imageAlt: Dr. Neda Moezzi, DDS, in her Valencia office

intro.heading: Treating the cause, not just the ache
paragraphs: The temporomandibular joint, or TMJ, is the hinge that connects your lower jaw to your skull. It works every time you chew, speak or yawn. When the joint or the muscles around it are strained, injured or out of alignment, the result is a TMJ disorder, often shortened to TMD. Common causes include grinding or clenching, a misaligned bite, stress, arthritis in the joint and injury to the jaw or face.

Dr. Moezzi takes an integrative view of TMJ care. Rather than only masking symptoms, she looks for what is driving them, whether that is nighttime clenching, worn teeth or muscle tension, and builds a plan around it. Treatment may include a custom night guard, Botox to relax overactive jaw muscles, bite adjustments or practical guidance on posture and stress. Patients from Valencia and across Santa Clarita come to us for this calm, thorough approach.

whoItsFor.heading: Who it's for
whoItsFor.intro: Occasional jaw tension is common, but frequent or worsening symptoms deserve a closer look.
items: Frequent jaw pain or stiffness, often in the morning or after chewing
Clicking, popping or locking when you open or close your mouth
Recurring headaches or earaches that seem to start in the jaw or temples
Pain or limited movement when biting or chewing firmer foods
Nighttime grinding or clenching, often noticed first by a partner
Neck or shoulder pain from muscle tension that spreads beyond the jaw

benefits.heading: What treatment can do for you
benefits.intro: Addressing a TMJ disorder tends to improve more than just your jaw.

items.title: Less pain
items.text: Targeted treatment can reduce jaw tension, headaches and muscle soreness linked to TMJ disorders.

items.title: Smoother jaw movement
items.text: Many patients find speaking, chewing and yawning more comfortable once the joint is under less strain.

items.title: Better sleep
items.text: Night guards and other appliances help limit grinding and clenching, so you and your teeth rest easier.

items.title: Protection for teeth and gums
items.text: Reducing grinding and uneven bite pressure helps prevent long-term wear and damage.

items.title: Everyday ease
items.text: With less pain and tension, daily activities feel simpler again.

options.heading: TMJ treatment options
options.intro: Dr. Moezzi combines these as needed to relieve pain, protect your teeth and restore balance.

items.title: Custom night guards
items.text: A precisely fitted guard worn during sleep that cushions grinding and clenching, easing pressure on the joint and protecting your teeth from wear.

items.title: Botox for TMJ relief
items.text: Targeted injections relax overactive jaw muscles, which can reduce pain, tension and strain on the joint.

items.title: Sleep apnea and oral devices
items.text: Custom appliances that support nighttime breathing and can also lessen the clenching and grinding that aggravate TMJ symptoms.

items.title: Bite adjustments and restorative care
items.text: Correcting how your teeth meet or rebuilding worn teeth restores balanced function and takes stress off the jaw joint.

items.title: Lifestyle and stress guidance
items.text: Practical strategies for posture, relaxation and daily habits that reduce TMJ triggers and support long-term comfort.

process.heading: What to expect
process.intro: Relief starts with understanding your symptoms and building a plan that fits your life.

steps.title: Comprehensive evaluation
steps.text: Dr. Moezzi examines your jaw, bite and muscles, reviews your medical history and may take digital X-rays or 3D CBCT images of the joint to pinpoint the source of your discomfort.

steps.title: A personalized plan
steps.text: Based on what she finds, Dr. Moezzi designs a plan that may combine an oral appliance, Botox therapy, bite adjustment and holistic recommendations. You will understand each step and why it is included.

steps.title: Ongoing care and support
steps.text: Follow-up visits track your progress so treatment can be fine-tuned. You get at-home guidance along the way, and the aim is steady, durable improvement in comfort and function.

technology.heading: Diagnostics that find the source
technology.intro: Accurate imaging and digital records lead to appliances that fit and plans that work.

items.title: 3D CBCT imaging
items.text: Three-dimensional scans show the jaw joint and surrounding bone in detail when a closer look is needed.

items.title: iTero digital scanner
items.text: Digital impressions capture your bite accurately for a night guard or oral appliance that fits well.

items.title: Digital X-rays
items.text: Low-radiation images help assess your teeth, bite and joint at your first visit.

faqs.q: What are the most common symptoms of TMJ disorders?
faqs.a: The most common signs are jaw pain or stiffness, clicking or popping sounds when you open and close, headaches and earaches, and difficulty chewing or opening wide. Some patients also notice discomfort spreading to the neck and shoulders, because the jaw muscles connect to those areas.

faqs.q: How do I know if I need TMJ treatment?
faqs.a: Occasional jaw tension is normal, but ongoing discomfort, trouble chewing, frequent headaches or a jaw that clicks or locks are worth evaluating. Getting assessed early can help prevent worn teeth and longer-term joint problems. Dr. Moezzi can tell you whether treatment makes sense or whether watchful waiting is enough.

Most TMJ treatments are non-invasive and intended to ease discomfort, not add to it. Night guards and oral appliances are custom fitted, bite adjustments are minor and can be done with local anesthesia if needed, and Botox injections involve brief, small needle sticks that most patients tolerate well.

faqs.q: How long does it take to see results from TMJ treatment?
faqs.a: It varies. Some patients notice improvement within a few weeks of wearing a night guard or receiving Botox, while others take longer, depending on the severity of the condition and the elements of the plan. Dr. Moezzi monitors your progress at follow-up visits and adjusts treatment as needed.

Coverage for TMJ treatment varies widely by provider and plan. Some cover oral appliances, some cover a portion of other therapies and some exclude TMJ care altogether. Our team will review your benefits, explain what is included and help you explore financing options if needed.
